name: Tarocco Siciliano — the Sicilian Tarot
description:
# Tarocco Siciliano

## At a glance

The tarot pack of Sicily, still used for the game of Sicilian tarocchi. It has 63 cards: twenty numbered trumps,
the Miseria below them, the Fool (the Fugitive), and four suits in which only the cards from 5 to 10 and the four
courts remain, with a 4 kept in coins [@web_pagat_sicilian]. A 64th card, the ace of coins, was added in the
19th century to carry the tax stamp [@web_pagat_sicilian].

## Where it comes from

Tarot reached Sicily in the mid-17th century, probably from Rome, as the 97-card Gallerini (the Minchiate) and a
78-card tarocchi; by the 1780s the pack was being shortened, and the 63-card pack became the standard
[@web_pagat_sicilian]. Several trumps borrow their pictures from the Minchiate [@web_wp_tarocco_siciliano].

## What is its own

- **Trumps found nowhere else:** Miseria, a chained beggar below trump 1; Constancy (4) with her flag; the Ship (14);
  Atlas with the globe (19); Jupiter as the highest trump (20). There is no Devil [@web_wp_tarocco_siciliano].
- **Names lost:** players call trumps 2 to 15 by number; only the old names of 4, 14 and 15 are known
  [@web_wp_tarocco_siciliano].
- **Women knaves:** the lowest court in each suit is a maid, so the pack has two ranks of women
  [@web_wp_tarocco_siciliano].
- **Portuguese suits:** knobbly clubs and straight swords that cross, the last tarot with this form of the Latin suits
  [@web_wp_tarocco_siciliano].

## In this library

The 21 trumps (twenty numbered, and the Miseria) and the Fool, with pictures where an open one exists. The 41 suit cards are still to be added.

## Where the pictures come from

Five trumps (Miseria, Constancy, Ship, Moon, Jupiter) are scans of a 1966 Modiano pack, filed on Wikimedia Commons as
public domain (PD-old-70); the pattern itself settled in the early 19th century. A printed pack from 1966 is a weak
case for public domain, so these are listed among the flagged images. The Fool and the cover are photographs by
Wikimedia users under CC BY-SA 4.0 (Riccardo ricceri; Countakeshi). The other trumps have no open picture yet.

Unnumbered and unlabelled. In play it cannot lead a trick unless it is the last trick [@web_wp_tarocco_siciliano]; it is worth 10 points [@web_wp_tarocco_siciliano].
